text:
It is not your fault if in your hands

my love lost its petals like a rose:

Spring will come and there will be flowers...

the dry trunk will give new leaves.


The tears shed will become pearls

of a new necklace; shadow will be broken by

a precious sun that will give to the veins

fresh sap, mad and bubbling.


You will follow your route; I mine

and both, freed, like butterflies

will lose the pollen from our wings

and find more pollen in the flora.


Words dry up like rivers

and kisses dry up like roses,

but for every death seven lives

seek lips demanding dawn.


But... what was? It is never recovered!

And every spring that sketches itself

is one more corpse that acquires life

and one more bud that loses its petals!

translation.title: The Endless
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the regenerative argument and the final refusal of full recovery.
